newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Douwe Egberts raises Dutch retail coffee price.
newsitem.headline: Douwe Egberts raises Dutch retail coffee price.

text.p: Douwe Egberts, the leading Dutch coffee roaster, said on Thursday it had raised the retail price of coffee due to the explosive rally in world prices.

The latest rise would take the average shop price in the Netherlands for a standard 250-gramme pack of coffee to 4.30 guilders, up from four guilders, spokesman Joost den Haan told Reuters. Douwe Egberts is part of the Sara Lee Corporation of the United States.
"There are fears over the frosts (in Brazil) and we have seen huge demand on the futures market. There is a higher dollar rate against the guilder," Den Haan said.
The company last raised the Dutch retail price on May 7, when the average went up by 20 cents to four guilders.

World raw coffee prices have spiralled to 20-year highs on a powerful mix of tight supplies from Latin America, concerns over the potential for crop-damaging frosts in Brazil and extremely low stock levels in consumer countries.
Asked if Douwe Egberts was concerned about being unable to get hold of the premium arabica coffee supplies it needed for its blends, Den Haan said:
"Stocks are low and we are worried about the world price but there is no reason to think that will happen."
Douwe Egberts hold some 70 percent of the Dutch market.

In New York on Thursday arabica coffee futures soared above $3 per pound for the first time in 20 years and in London robustas put on almost 15 percent in a few frenzied hours to rise above $2,500 per tonne, double where they began 1997.
